text:
emma: New hire reported a surprising mypy/pyright error when subclassing generated models in the sample app. Autogen runtime gives Pydantic BaseModel instances but the .pyi stubs export TypedDicts for those models, so you can't subclass them in type-checked code. Blocking a demo today.

rick: Ouch. Can you paste the repro? Which type checker/version?

emma: repro (mypy 1.9.0 + pyright strict):

```py
# sampleapp trying to extend an autogen model
from redwood.models import Widget  # runtime: Widget is pydantic BaseModel

class RichWidget(Widget):  # mypy/pyright error: "TypedDict" is not a class
    extra: str

w = RichWidget(name="x", size=3, extra="meta")
print(w.extra)
```

emma: Errors: "Cannot subclass TypedDict" / "Expression produces a TypedDict" depending on checker. Runtime works (object created) but type-checkers reject it. New hires expect to extend models for small wrapper logic.

juan: We've historically emitted TypedDicts in stubs for model shapes because they surface keys nicely in editors and are lightweight. But that doesn't model the runtime which is an actual class. That's a mismatch.

priya: Two paths: 1) change pyi generation to emit actual class stubs that inherit from pydantic.BaseModel (class Widget(BaseModel): name: str; size: int), which allows subclassing and preserves attribute lookup; or 2) document that autogenerated model types are TypedDicts and provide a typed wrapper base class users can import to extend (e.g., WidgetModel = pydantic.BaseModel subclass).

rick: Which is less breaking? Emitting classes in pyi to match runtime seems right but could be tricky if we don't want to import pydantic in stub files. We could write class stubs with no runtime imports using 'from typing import Any' and simple annotations; editors and type-checkers will treat them as classes.

juan: We can generate minimal class stubs that subclass 'pydantic.BaseModel' in the pyi (or if we want to avoid dependency, subclass 'object' but add docstring saying runtime is pydantic). Subclassing will work either way for typing. The main benefit is ergonomic: users can subclass and IDEs show attributes.

priya: Risk: some users run in environments without pydantic installed (we vendor a tiny runtime adapter sometimes). If pyi references pydantic.BaseModel, pyright may complain in environments lacking that package. But type checkers usually ignore missing runtime imports if types are available or can be installed in dev envs.

emma: For onboarding, the simplest fix is to generate class-based stubs that mirror runtime classes (no TypedDict). That unblocks subclassing and attribute access. We can follow up with a doc note about pydantic dependency for dev-time typing.

rick: Agreed. Let's do: autogen pyi -> emit 'class Widget: name: str; size: int' OR 'class Widget(BaseModel): ...' depending on config; default to plain class stub inheriting from 'object' to avoid a hard pydantic import, but include a comment in the stub: '# runtime is pydantic.BaseModel'. That should satisfy both mypy and pyright.

juan: Also add a test in sampleapp CI where someone subclasses a generated model to ensure future regressions are caught. And add a short snippet in the onboarding doc explaining the difference and recommended pattern for lightweight subclassing.

priya: I'll open a GH issue and label eng-ml + devex. Please include the minimal repro and CI logs.

emma: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3345 1: reproducer + suggested pyi generation change.

devx-bot: Issue created: #3345 by @emma 1: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/3345 :white_check_mark:

rick: I'll take the autogen template change. Plan: 1) update pyi generator to emit class stubs (object-subclass by default), 2) add sampleapp subclassing test, 3) update docs + add a migration note, 4) consider opt-in to explicitly reference pydantic.BaseModel in stubs for users who want full fidelity.

juan: Note: also check codegen for enum/TypedDict edgecases so we don't regress similar mismatches.

emma: Thanks all, this will stop blocking demos. Appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
